answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a small, time-locked bond before it may influence reputation-weighted decisions. A pulse of activity from many fresh accounts then carries little weight until those bonds have aged and the accounts have earned trust through repeated, useful work. An attacker can still create sybils, but must tie up capital for each one and risk losing it if the account is caught coordinating abuse; timber and ferrous goods are irrelevant unless the system accepts them as collateral.
